On the boundary you asked about — yes, that's the right line for me. If I type "recipes" and I already have "Recipes," those are plainly the same label to me and it should just reuse the one I've got rather than spawning a near-identical twin that only differs by a capital letter — that's exactly the mess I was worried about earlier. But I wouldn't want it going further and *guessing* that genuinely different words like "recipe" and "Recipes" are the same thing; that kind of guessing would eventually merge things I meant to keep apart. Matching on wording that's identical apart from capitalization is the sensible place to stop.

One thing, though: the screen you gave me doesn't actually show me that happening. What I'm looking at is the editor open on the title and description, and the card behind it only shows the "Work" label — I can't see the label picker reusing "Recipes," the little note saying it reused it, or the finished card carrying both Work and Recipes with no lowercase duplicate. So I can't confirm the result itself from this.

Could you show me the state where I've typed "recipes," it's told me it reused the existing one, and then the saved card with both labels? Once I can see that, I expect I'll be happy — the rule behind it is right.
